Leaky RND on ICM-φ

A lineage of sparse-reward exploration experiments on ARC-style games — what we built, what worked, what broke, the fixes we tried, and what the results actually say.

1 · The problem & why we needed a new method

We study exploration in reward-sparse environments. The single quantity we care about is env_steps_to_first_reward — how many environment interactions (summed across all parallel actors) an agent needs before its first positive extrinsic reward (= its first successful trajectory). We do not care how good it becomes afterward.

This reframes RL completely: during learning there is effectively no extrinsic reward to optimize — the first +1 ends the run. The entire problem is shaping an intrinsic signal so the agent stumbles onto a success as fast as possible. We measure this across a grid of 4 ARC-engine games × 3 early levels (ls20, tu93, re86, g50t), dropping the agent directly into level k, stopping on first reward, and right-censoring at a per-cell step cap.

The baseline that defines "hard"

A uniform-random policy reaches the reward in finite expected time in only 4 of the 12 cells: tu93 L2 ≈ 2k, ls20 L1 ≈ 50k, tu93 L1 ≈ 500k, re86 L1 ≈ 2M steps. Every other cell is E = ∞ — undirected exploration never finds the goal within any practical budget. On those "beat-the-impossible" cells a single solve is the whole result; on the finite cells the method has to beat random's expectation.

So we need directed exploration, and we need it to keep working long enough to reach the first reward. That is the bar the whole lineage is trying to clear.

2 · The two standard baselines and how each one fails

Before inventing anything we implemented the two canonical intrinsic-motivation methods faithfully, measured exactly how each one fails on these games, and used those failure modes as the design spec for "ours."

ICM (Pathak 2017) — curiosity collapse

exp_011: forward-dynamics prediction error as the bonus, separate inverse-dynamics encoder φ, η auto-calibrated once on the first (untrained) rollout and then frozen. The failure is mechanical and we traced it to the checkpoint level:

  • η is calibrated against the untrained forward error (~23) → η ≈ 3e-4, then frozen.
  • The forward model learns in ~2 updates; error falls ~60× → the bonus mechanically falls ~60× to ~6e-5 — 1–2 orders of magnitude below the PPO entropy floor. Right direction, far too small to reshape the policy.
  • On L1 ICM solved 2/3 seeds (it found the goal inside the brief curiosity-alive window, then PPO took over). On L2 all 3/3 seeds: 0% success, first reward never found — the window closes long before a ~60-action solution can be stumbled into.

A separate probe (exp_012_2) tested whether a k-step ICM reward would help: it doesn't — k-step error is just a ×4–5 copy of 1-step error that η renormalizes away, with no gain in cross-state discrimination. Horizon is not the lever.

RND (Burda 2018) — saturation that never revives

exp_012: distillation error of a predictor chasing a fixed random target. Two measured failures:

  • One-way ratchet. Once the predictor fits a state's random target, that state's novelty collapses toward machine-zero permanently. Re-visited states stop producing any reward → exploration stalls. On a long run the novelty field flattens by ~80k steps and the agent bleeds entropy on an effectively-rewardless objective.
  • No count resolution on pixels + a 99.9% leak. On raw frames, per-state error is ~3e-4 at 1 visit and ~1–2e-4 at 2000 visits (1 visit ≈ 2000 visits); and a never-visited holdout state's error drops 99.9% purely from training on other states — near-identical maze frames make the random target smooth, so the predictor interpolates novelty everywhere.

The design spec, written from the failures

ICM collapses (bonus decays with the learner's own accuracy); RND saturates (one-way ratchet) and has no resolution on pixels (it leaks). A good method has to fix collapse, saturation, resolution/leak, and the reward-time lag at once — while staying generalizable (no exact-frame hashing).

3 · The idea: Optimistic Curiosity Control — leaky RND on ICM-φ

The unifying lens is optimism in the face of uncertainty: act on a value plus a shrinking confidence width. Curiosity is that width. Two ideas combine the baselines' strengths while patching their failures:

  1. Run RND inside ICM's inverse-dynamics feature space φ, not on pixels. The IDM must separate states that pixels conflate (it has to predict the action between them), which removes the pixel-smoothness leak and restores count resolution. φ is frozen once inverse_acc saturates, because φ never self-stabilizes (see §5) and RND needs a stationary ruler.
  2. Make the RND predictor "leaky." After each update, shrink it toward its random init: θ ← (1−μ)·θ + μ·θ_init (decoupled from Adam, not a loss term). This creates a tug-of-war: distillation pulls error down on currently-visited states; the leak drags weights back toward init everywhere. States you keep visiting win and stay low-error; states you abandon drift back up and become "novel again." RND stops measuring cumulative count and starts measuring recent visitation rate — so it never permanently saturates.

Novelty enters only through the reward channel (one scale; TD learns the rest), with a single intrinsic-only value head and non-episodic GAE (novelty value bootstraps across death — the agent isn't deterred from life-costing deep exploration). The extrinsic +1 is the stop signal only, never fed to GAE.

Two further arms were built but not part of the leaky-RND lineage proper: D = an actor-free MCTS 1-step-lookahead-softmax (a structural fix for the entropy collapse), and E = Plan2Explore ensemble disagreement (a non-redundant signal). Both smoke-pass; D benched ~7× slower than random on the cheapest cell, so neither was promoted.

4 · What the leak actually does — our cleanest positive result

The leak is the central innovation, and it is the one thing in the whole lineage that works exactly as designed, with clean, controlled, reproducible evidence. We isolated it three different ways, all on real LS20-L2 visitation data with the production RND engine and our timer-masked board identity.

The non-obvious tuning that made this honest

The literal "one single-sample Adam distill step per env step" at lr=1e-3 is treacherous: it causes catastrophic interference that lifts the abandoned states even at μ=0, masking the leak as the cause of forgetting. The clean result required rnd_lr=1e-4 (gentle steps) + proj_dim=1024 (more orthogonal features ⇒ less cross-state generalization). And the crucial cadence fact: the real loop leaks once per PPO update (~2048 env-steps), not per step — a per-step μ=0.05 is ~2048× too aggressive and pegs every state to init. Equivalent per-step rate ≈ μupdate / 2048.

5 · What broke — five diagnoses

The leak works in isolation. The trouble is everything around it on the real training runs. Five separate probes localized five distinct problems. This is most of the intellectual content of the project.

5.1 · Entropy collapse → worse-than-random

On ls20 L1, variant B solved only 1/3 seeds and the outcome was perfectly rank-ordered by policy entropy: seed2 (H≈1.34, near-uniform) solved at 24k; seed1 (H≈0.81) censored; seed0 (H→0.000 for ~60k steps, a fully deterministic loop) censored. A single knob — raising c_entropy 0.01→0.05 — flipped the worst seed from censored-at-250k to solved-at-33k. Coverage ≠ solving: a real-engine probe showed that as entropy falls from ln4→0.2, the rate of hitting the mandatory rotation tile drops ~6×.

5.2 · The collapse has two mechanisms, on different cells

A sharp control settled the cause: replacing the reward channel with zero (H floors ~1.0) or noise (H stays ~1.36) does not collapse entropy — only the real novelty reward does. And uncomfortably, the dual-head RND baseline collapses hardest of all (6/8 re86 seeds → H≈0), so the architecture isn't what protects you. The honest synthesis: this is the same "phantom-advantage-from-an-informative-signal" pathology we first hit with a JEPA-pretrained critic in exp_010.

5.3 · φ never becomes a trustworthy ruler — and the freeze trigger was fooled

5.4 · The observation confound — a marching step-timer 🔴

The single most damaging bug, present since exp_010: the env wrapper masks the UI rows (energy / step-timer, ls20 rows 60–63) only in its diff utilities, not in the frame fed to the models. So a step-timer marches one cell every step regardless of the agent — making every frame unique (1073 "distinct" raw frames vs 43 distinct board states after masking). The clock swamps the novelty signal and quietly poisoned every count/RND result, and is a likely reason φ never became controllable.

5.5 · The additive idea (C) is dead — signals are anti-informative

Before spending a 500k-step weight-sweep on C, a free probe killed it. On ls20 L2, correlating each signal with the true visitation oracle (−log count on masked frames):

quantityvaluereading
corr(ICM-fwd, −log count)−0.46reward is higher on more-visited states
corr(RND-on-φ, −log count)−0.56also backwards
corr(ICM, RND) within-update≈ +0.24moderately redundant
no-op (wall-bump) fraction0.49~half of transitions don't change the board
distinct masked states reached43coverage collapse

Both signals correlate negatively with true novelty. No convex weight w·(−0.46) + (1−w)·(−0.56) can be positive — combining two anti-informative rulers stays anti-informative for every w. The 500k sweep was cancelled. The binding constraint is φ-controllability + the observation confound, not the ICM-vs-RND mix.

6 · The fixes we tried

fixtargetsoutcome
Method-specific normalizer: ICM gets warm-up=3 (zero reward while φ burns in) + EMA-std; RND keeps its paper-faithful cumulative RMS. ICM's untrained ~700× startup transient poisoning the shared normalizer (crushed the bonus to ~1e-4 for ~43k steps). Worked. ls20-L1 ICM went from censored >92k → 18.8k. The clearest harness-level fix.
Leaky predictor (μ shrink-to-init).RND saturation / one-way ratchet. Worked mechanically (§4) — but not load-bearing for any solve yet (see §7).
Held-out-inv_acc freeze trigger + a hard guard "never freeze while holdout < 1.5×chance," and decouple the u100 step-fallback. The fooled on-policy freeze (§5.3) that pinned a chance-level φ as the RND ruler (drove re86 entropy→0.000). Partial. Correct fix; the gate is only reachable on g50t and only as the run ends — re86 φ is structurally uncontrollable at this budget, so the real answer is to route re86-like cells to frozen-φ (A).
Timer mask on the novelty/count path (rows 60–63).The marching-clock observation confound (§5.4). Applied in probes; folded into the masked sweep. The pre-mask baseline data is flagged "confounded."
Value-lag mitigations: reward clip before the normalizer, γ_int 0.99→0.95, c_value 0.5→1.0, c_entropy 0.01→0.10. The phantom-advantage collapse regime (§5.2 left). Band-aids. Raise the floor the phantom advantage must overcome; they don't remove the lag. A big enough novelty burst still overruns any fixed coefficient.
Checkpointing + richer logging (clipfrac, V vs Ret, holdout_inv_acc, novelty_raw_max). The analysis gap — no checkpoints existed to roll out the trained policy.Done.

The honest read of these numbers

  • On the cells where there's headroom, the leaky variants are competitive and sometimes have the lowest median (A on ls20-L1 20k, A on tu93-L1 69k, B on re86-L1 90k, B on g50t-L1 61k) — but with 2–4 seeds against a p≈8.6e-4 process, these differences are within seed variance, not demonstrated speedups.
  • No cell shows the leaky design clearly beating the RND/ICM baselines in a way the seed count can support. And on the one genuinely deep tractable cell, tu93 L3, plain ICM is the only method that solves it — its "collapse" there is productive (the policy converges onto the reward path), while every novelty-preserving method keeps exploring and never commits.
  • The leak's value is demonstrated mechanistically (§4) but not yet converted into a benchmark win, because the binding constraints on the hard cells are upstream of it: entropy collapse, φ-controllability, the observation confound, and — most fundamentally — zero reward coverage.

8 · Honest verdict & what's next

What worked

  • The leak is real and clean. Three independent controlled experiments (exp_014_1/2/5) show standard RND saturates permanently while leaky RND regenerates novelty by recency, μ-ordered and reproducible. This is the project's solid scientific contribution.
  • RND-on-φ beats RND-on-pixels in principle — pixels have no count resolution and a 99.9% leak; φ separates states.
  • The normalizer fix (warm-up + EMA for ICM) genuinely cured ICM's startup-transient collapse.
  • The diagnostics themselves. We now know precisely why each method fails and on which cell.

What didn't

  • The additive combination (C) is dead — anti-informative signals can't be mixed into an informative one.
  • The learned-φ ruler (B) is undermined by φ never becoming controllable on re86/ls20 — on those cells a frozen-random φ (A) is strictly better, so B's only edge is absent exactly where it's needed.
  • The leaky design never converts into a clear benchmark win — entropy collapse, the timer confound, and zero reward coverage on L2/L3 dominate whatever the leak buys.
  • The MCTS-lookahead arm (D) benched slower than random; its Q mis-ranks actions on these cells.

Ranked next steps (from the probe write-ups)

  1. Masked-frame count — the strongest unbuilt lever. Intrinsic reward = count novelty on UI-masked frames (43 stationary, informative states; 1/√N). No φ, no timer confound, directly fixes §5.3+§5.4.
  2. Attack reward coverage, not saturation — the L2/L3 bottleneck is that v_ext≡0 (the reward is never reached). Go-Explore-style directed return to the frontier is the real cure for coverage ≠ sequence.
  3. PopArt value normalization — the principled fix for the value-lag regime (§5.2 left): lets the critic track a non-stationary return without manufacturing phantom advantage.
  4. Entropy floor / KL-to-uniform — robust insurance against the dead-field bleed regime (§5.2 right), which no fixed c_entropy reliably stops.
  5. Ensemble disagreement (E) on masked frozen-φ — the non-redundant epistemic signal, with no stationary-ruler dependence.
